claims.claim: Five-statistic ridge predictor attains family-macro log MAE 0.181 on the sealed held-out graphs.
The 2m(n-1) bound attains family-macro log MAE 1.754 on the same graphs.
Difference between bound and ridge log MAE is 1.572.
Constant predictor (training geometric mean) attains family-macro log MAE 0.870.
Ridge predictions scored against shuffled targets give family-macro log MAE 1.423.
Ratios of constant, shuffled and bound log MAE to ridge log MAE are about 4.8, 7.8 and 9.7; exp() factors 1.20, 2.39, 4.15, 5.78 (arithmetic on reported values).
Median relative Monte Carlo standard error of test labels is 0.029 (about 2.9%), roughly 0.16 of the ridge log MAE.
Under a Gaussian approximation the label-noise-only expected absolute log error would be about 0.023, about 13% of 0.181 (derived arithmetic).
Worst-case concentration: no family mean log error exceeds 12 x 0.181 = 2.18 (factor about 8.8) and no single test graph exceeds 24 x 0.181 = 4.35 (factor about 78) (derived arithmetic).
Maximum relative deviation of predictions across relabeled copies is 0.0.
Three seeded episodes (seeds 201, 202, 203) each give score -0.18137 with durations of about 0.06 seconds; the spread across episodes is zero.
The sealed evaluation completed and its outcome is qualified; candidate diagnostics are unverified.
Selection context: the studied configuration is the retained reference; 1 alternative candidate, 0 scored, 1 unscored; investigation completed without a winner; search score delta 0.0.
Selection score of the retained configuration is -0.1913 on selection test graphs, a different evaluation scope from the sealed final metrics.

Protocol facts (36 training graphs, 24 test graphs, 12 families, about 300 walks, clip 10, tolerance 1e-6, seeds 201-203) describe the setting in which the sealed family-macro log MAE is computed; derived from protocol_inputs/ via protocol_facts.json.
Feige's upper bound (4/27+o(1))n^3 and lower bound (1+o(1)) n ln n on cover time of connected graphs.
Cover and hitting times have been derived for particular random graph models such as hyperbolic random graphs.
Aleliunas et al. showed the cover time from any start is at most 2m(n-1); the bound is the paper's headline comparator.
Lovász's survey collects hitting-time and commute-time machinery for random walks on graphs; Doyle and Snell give the electrical-network view relating commute times to effective resistances.

Analytic log overshoot of the 2m(n-1) bound: about 0.54 on the path at n=30, exactly ln 4 (about 1.39) on the cycle at every n, about 2.0 on the star and about 5.4 on the complete graph at n=30, so the bound is tight up to a constant factor on some graphs and overshoots by a growing factor on dense graphs (derived from closed-form cover times in closed_form_gap.json; the sealed bound comparator is final.metric.bound_macro_log_mae).
